label: Supply chain and logistics
description: The people who buy, make, move, store and recall goods: supply chain and procurement leaders, logistics and transportation managers, distribution center and cold storage operators, third-party logistics providers, food safety and quality teams who run recalls, and supply chain programs at universities. Three variants share one profile: a manufacturer or brand owner (supplier risk, allocation, sourcing), a distributor or third-party logistics provider (lanes, dock, inventory, carriers) and a food recall team (lot tracing, consignee notices, regulator contact). Enterprise resource planning, warehouse and transportation systems, EDI, shipment visibility and lot traceability sit under them. Every company, supplier, carrier and customer is fictional.

vocabulary.facility: the company's network (plants, distribution centers, cold storage, cross-docks and the lanes between them)
vocabulary.public: customers, retailers and food service accounts, patients and consumers who depend on the product
vocabulary.frontline: buyers, planners, dock and warehouse crews, drivers and dispatchers, quality technicians, customer service reps
vocabulary.operationsCenter: the supply chain control tower (or the recall command room), with the transportation and warehouse desks

it: enterprise resource planning (ERP) with demand and supply planning
warehouse management system (WMS) and transportation management system (TMS)
supplier portal, EDI and API links to suppliers, carriers and customers
shipment visibility (vessel, rail and truck tracking, telematics)
lot and batch traceability in the manufacturing execution system (MES), with label and barcode printing
customs and trade compliance software and the customs broker's filing system
supplier risk monitoring and spend analytics
email, identity and the managed service provider
ot: temperature monitoring: refrigeration controllers, data loggers and cold room alarms
conveyors, sortation and automated storage and retrieval
dock doors, yard management and gate scanners
backup power and generators for cold storage

roles.name: Chief Supply Chain Officer / VP Supply Chain (Incident Commander)
roles.description: Decides allocation among customers, expedite spend and alternate sources, and when to escalate to the CEO.

roles.name: Procurement / Sourcing Director
roles.description: Decides to switch to a second source, qualify a substitute, and the contract and price terms.

roles.name: Supplier Risk Manager
roles.description: Owns supplier status, tier-2 and tier-3 visibility and risk scores.

roles.name: Logistics / Transportation Manager
roles.description: Decides reroutes, mode changes (ocean to air), carrier selection and detention and demurrage.

roles.name: Distribution Center Manager
roles.description: Sets inbound and outbound priorities, labor, storage and quarantine areas.

roles.name: Inventory / Demand Planner
roles.description: Owns days of supply by item and site, rebalances inventory and resets the forecast.

roles.name: Food Safety and Quality Assurance Lead
roles.description: Holds product, supplies health hazard input and recommends a recall.

roles.name: Recall Coordinator
roles.description: Sets recall strategy depth, runs the lot trace, owns the consignee list and effectiveness checks.

roles.name: Customer Service / Key Account Manager
roles.description: Sends customer notices and allocation messages and negotiates service credits.

roles.name: General Counsel / Regulatory Affairs
roles.description: Owns regulator contact, force majeure positions and public statements.

roles.name: Communications Lead (PIO)
roles.description: Writes the recall notice, customer letters and media statements.

roles.name: IT / Logistics Systems Lead (Technical Lead)
roles.description: Restores the transportation and warehouse systems and EDI connections.

outsideParties: suppliers at tiers one to three
carriers, freight forwarders and third-party logistics providers
customers: retail, wholesale, food service and hospital accounts
the FDA or USDA FSIS, and the state and local health departments
the insurer and the insurance broker
the cyber insurer, an incident response firm and CISA (for a logistics cyber attack)
the county emergency management agency (for a regional supply disruption)
mediaChannels: trade press and freight news sites
retailer and customer social posts about empty shelves
consumer posts on X and Reddit about a recalled product
a LinkedIn post by a laid-off supplier employee

sceneAnchors.public: a grocery aisle with a half-empty shelf and a handwritten limit sign, a shopper reading a label, a store employee restocking from a pallet, bright fluorescent light
sceneAnchors.control: a supply chain control tower: planners at long desks with laptops, a wall of shipment maps and bar charts, headsets, coffee cups, a whiteboard with lane names
sceneAnchors.exterior: a distribution center yard: rows of trailers backed to dock doors, a gate shack, a line of trucks waiting, a forklift at a loading bay, overcast daylight

addedThreatFamilies.label: Supplier failure or supply shock
addedThreatFamilies.description: A source the company depends on stops shipping (fire, bankruptcy, labor action, sanctions, a price spike); the team protects days of supply, allocates what is left and qualifies another source.

phaseArc.title: Signal
phaseArc.goal: The first sign is small and arrives from the edge of the network, not from the supplier's own notice.
beats: A buyer hears from a carrier that a supplier's dock is closed
A supplier portal status that has not updated in two days
A tier-2 mill mentioned in a trade press item that nobody here knew was in the chain

phaseArc.title: Verify and size
phaseArc.goal: The team confirms what is lost and for how long, and learns how many days of supply sit where.
beats: A force majeure letter with a vague restart date
A days-of-supply dashboard where the plant with the least stock is not the plant with the most urgent orders
Stock counted in the wrong location in the ERP

phaseArc.title: Protect supply
phaseArc.goal: Allocation, expedite and alternate-source choices each have a cost and a clock.
beats: A request to qualify a second source that needs a quality audit first
A key customer demanding priority and a contract clause that backs them
An expedite quote that eats the quarter's margin

phaseArc.title: Communicate
phaseArc.goal: Customers, the board and the sales team hear the same facts in the same order.
beats: A sales director promising a ship date the plan cannot meet
A customer reading about the failure in the trade press before hearing from the company

phaseArc.title: Recover and learn
phaseArc.goal: Supply returns in stages and the team decides what to change in sourcing.
beats: The supplier restarts at half capacity
A debate on dual sourcing against the cost of holding stock

decisionPointExamples: Allocate the remaining stock by contract priority or by customer criticality
Pay for air freight on a share of the order or accept a stock-out week
Qualify a second source now at a quality risk, or wait for the audit
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a supplier portal status, a carrier remark, a force majeure letter, a days-of-supply row that falls below the reorder point, a sales order that cannot be filled
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: the alternate source is not qualified, the bill of materials hides a tier-2 dependency, the ERP shows stock that is not physically there, customers hold contract allocation rights
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the sole-source supplier's account manager, key customers, the alternate source, a freight forwarder

decisionMustMention.description: name the allocation, expedite or alternate-source choice and what it costs

addedThreatFamilies.label: Port, rail or lane disruption
addedThreatFamilies.description: A port, rail line, highway, canal or channel closes or clogs; shipments slip, containers pile up and the team reroutes, changes mode or accepts stock-outs.

phaseArc.title: Signal
phaseArc.goal: A closure or a blockage is reported, and its effect on this company's freight is not yet clear.
beats: A carrier advisory about a closed lane
A vessel tracker showing a ship holding at anchor
A customs broker asking whether to hold a filing

phaseArc.title: Map the exposure
phaseArc.goal: The team lists which shipments, containers and trailers sit behind the disruption and what each is carrying.
beats: A shipment tracker where half the exceptions are coded 'delayed' with no reason
Two containers of a critical item on different vessels
A customer order with a promised date inside the delay

phaseArc.title: Reroute or accept
phaseArc.goal: Mode change, alternate port, expedited truck and reallocation each cost money and shift the risk.
beats: An ocean-to-air quote for a small share of the load
Detention and demurrage meters running at a terminal
A rail ramp that is open but without chassis

phaseArc.title: Communicate
phaseArc.goal: Customers receive revised dates they can plan against.
beats: Two account managers giving different revised dates
A retailer asking whether to cancel the promotion

phaseArc.title: Recover
phaseArc.goal: Backlog clears unevenly and the team decides how much safety stock to rebuild.
beats: A surge of arrivals that overwhelms the receiving dock
A cost review that questions the expedite spend

decisionPointExamples: Switch the critical item to air freight at a high cost, or accept a three-week stock-out
Divert vessels to another port and accept a longer trucking leg
Tell customers a revised date now, or wait until the carrier commits
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a lane or port advisory, a vessel or trailer position, an ETA that slips between two updates, a dwell-time figure, a demurrage invoice
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: no chassis or drivers at the alternate port, the alternate lane is also congested, the carrier will not commit to a date, free-time clocks expire
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the carrier or ocean line, the port or terminal, the customs broker, the freight forwarder

decisionMustMention.description: name the reroute, mode change or accepted delay

addedThreatFamilies.label: Product safety, cold chain and recall
addedThreatFamilies.description: A contaminated lot, a cold chain breach or a labeling error means finding every shipment of the affected product, deciding the recall's depth and notifying every consignee on a clock.

phaseArc.title: Signal
phaseArc.goal: A complaint, a test result, a supplier notice or a regulator call opens the question; it can arrive at any step.
beats: A retailer complaint with a lot code half legible on the photo
A positive result from a routine environmental swab
A call from a state inspector asking where a product went

phaseArc.title: Hold and investigate
phaseArc.goal: Product is held, the health hazard is evaluated and the quality team decides how far to look.
beats: Inventory in three distribution centers that has already shipped in part
A lab that cannot confirm until tomorrow
A tempting argument that only one lot is involved

phaseArc.title: Trace
phaseArc.goal: The recall coordinator builds the ship-to list from shipping and receiving records, against a records request clock.
beats: A shipping record missing its reference document
A lot code that changes format at a transformation step
A distributor who repacked and relabeled

phaseArc.title: Decide and notify
phaseArc.goal: Class, depth, public warning and effectiveness checks are chosen, and every direct account gets a letter marked urgent where the class requires it.
beats: A draft letter missing the lot numbers or the instructions
A decision on whether to warn the public now
A customer asking whether they can sell through

phaseArc.title: Retrieve and verify
phaseArc.goal: Product comes back; effectiveness checks show who has not answered.
beats: Accounts that have not replied after two days
Product already sold to consumers at retail
A status report due to the regulator with counts that disagree with the tracing spreadsheet

phaseArc.title: Root cause and restart
phaseArc.goal: The cause is found, corrective action is documented and the line restarts on a stated rule.
beats: A disagreement about whether to restart before the audit
An insurer asking for the timeline

decisionPointExamples: Recall to the consumer level with a public warning, or to the retail level without one
Send recall letters now with an incomplete ship-to list, or wait a day to complete it
Reply to the records request within the clock with known gaps, or ask the regulator for more time
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a lot code on a complaint photo, a lab result, a data logger alert, a shipping record with a missing field, a consignee list with a duplicate account
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: records on paper or in two systems, mismatched lot codes across a transformation, repackaged product, accounts that do not answer, a restart pressure from sales
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the regulator (FDA or USDA FSIS), the state health department, distributors and retailers, the insurer
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Stay at coordination level: lot codes, quantities, dates, ship-to lists, classes and letters. Do not write pathogen handling, culturing or sampling procedure detail.

decisionMustMention.description: name the recall, hold, depth or notification choice

addedThreatFamilies.label: Logistics provider or warehouse system cyber attack
addedThreatFamilies.description: A carrier, a third-party logistics provider or the company's own warehouse or transportation system is down; orders cannot ship and nobody is sure what has already left.

phaseArc.title: Signal
phaseArc.goal: Orders stop flowing and the first explanation is a network glitch.
beats: EDI acknowledgements that stop arriving
A warehouse supervisor reporting that scanners will not log in
A carrier call center that cannot look up a load

phaseArc.title: Contain and size
phaseArc.goal: The team learns which systems and which partners are affected and what shipped in the last day.
beats: A provider's notice that says only 'service interruption'
Pick lists printed from a stale cache
A second carrier asking the company to stop sending files

phaseArc.title: Operate manually
phaseArc.goal: Shipping continues on paper or stops, and every manual choice creates a record gap.
beats: Paper bills of lading with no lot code
A priority customer whose order is mid-pick
Drivers waiting at the gate without paperwork

phaseArc.title: Communicate
phaseArc.goal: Customers and partners get the same plain statement about what is delayed.
beats: A customer asking whether their data was taken
A press inquiry about a named provider

phaseArc.title: Restore and reconcile
phaseArc.goal: Systems come back and records are rebuilt, with traceability gaps closed.
beats: Duplicate shipments created at restart
A lot that cannot be tied to a ship-to without the paper

decisionPointExamples: Ship priority orders by hand without lot-level records, or hold them until the system returns
Cut the connection to the provider now, or keep it open to protect in-transit loads
Tell all customers a delay is expected, or only the affected ones
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: an EDI acknowledgement that does not arrive, a provider status note, a printed pick list with the wrong date, a driver without a load number, a ransom note
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: no manual process for lot-level records, the provider will not share details, a restart that duplicates shipments, the backup is days old
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the logistics provider, carriers, major customers, the cyber insurer and CISA or the FBI

decisionMustMention.description: name the manual, hold or disconnect choice

addedThreatFamilies.label: Critical product shortage
addedThreatFamilies.description: A medical, food or industrial product the community depends on runs short; the team allocates, substitutes and communicates under pressure from customers and the public.

phaseArc.title: Signal
phaseArc.goal: Orders outrun supply; backorders appear before the cause is clear.
beats: A backorder report that doubles in a week
Customers asking for larger shipments than usual
A news item about a plant closure upstream

phaseArc.title: Size the gap
phaseArc.goal: The team estimates demand, stock and recovery date and learns where the stock is.
beats: Inventory held at a customer that is not reported
A forecast built on pre-shortage demand
A substitute that is not interchangeable for every use

phaseArc.title: Allocate
phaseArc.goal: A stated rule decides who gets product; each choice is defended.
beats: A hospital asking for priority over a retailer
A contract clause that guarantees a customer a fixed share
A rule that is applied differently by two account managers

phaseArc.title: Communicate
phaseArc.goal: Customers and the public hear what is available, to whom and why.
beats: Customers hoarding after the first notice
A regulator asking for the allocation rule in writing

phaseArc.title: Recover
phaseArc.goal: Supply rebuilds and the allocation is lifted in a stated sequence.
beats: A false sense of recovery from one good week
A review of safety stock policy

decisionPointExamples: Allocate by historical share or by clinical or community need
Release the safety stock now or hold it for the weeks ahead
Allow a substitute that is not a full match, with a warning
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a backorder report, a days-of-supply row, a customer order inflated above history, a regulator request, a substitute product data sheet
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: demand is unreported, substitutes are not interchangeable, a contract guarantees share, news coverage drives hoarding
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: priority customers (hospitals, food banks), the regulator, distributors, the trade press

decisionMustMention.description: state the allocation rule or the substitution choice

noiseExamples: a purchase order with the wrong ship-to address
a driver disputing a detention charge
a customer asking about an unrelated backorder
a barcode label that will not scan on one pallet
a carrier rate increase notice effective next quarter
a freight invoice that does not match the bill of lading
pressureExamples: a key customer threatening to move volume to a competitor unless priority is confirmed
a retailer asking whether to pull product from shelves before the company has decided
a trade press reporter asking about a supplier the company has not yet named
a regulator asking for the ship-to list within the day
a board member asking why the company was not told about the tier-2 dependency
a social post claiming the product is unsafe, with a photo of the wrong lot
agencyPattern: FDA|USDA|FSIS|CBP|Customs|Coast Guard|Surface Transportation Board|Federal Maritime Commission|CISA|state health department
